title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: Price increase to $11.33
drivers.evidence: Two prior weeks at $11.33: sales 43 (x1.16) and 31 (x0.84); average x1.00, but 31 was 12% below baseline. No event, so price effect is plausible. Noise-adjusted estimate shrunk to x0.88 for 12% drop.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 36.9. The price increased 3.1% to $11.33, a level seen in two prior weeks (2026-03-30, 2026-04-06) with sales of 43 and 31, both below baseline. The prior week (2026-04-06) sold 31 units (x0.84 vs baseline), suggesting a price sensitivity effect. No promotion, event, or seasonality driver is present. The classical uplift model gives 1.00, but historical price hikes at this level show demand decline. Evidence is limited to two prior weeks at this price, so shrink effect toward 1.0. Median multiplier adjusted downward moderately.

brief:
PRODUCT: Cold & Flu Relief | category Health | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-04-13 to 2026-04-19 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 11.33 (+3.1% vs regular price 10.99)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 36.9 | 5%-95%: 25.5 - 52.7 | 10%-90%: 26.8 - 49.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-53% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
